authoredFrom: SQLD4 (M60 SQL wave, 2026-09-26). Arm-by-arm reachability measured with bb_tests/sql/probe/reachability.mts, which runs one probe per claimed switch arm and records whether the pattern or symbol the arm promises is ever emitted. Before: set_statement, reset_statement and comment_statement were unreachable (the grammar produces all three — probe/grammar-gaps.mts shows set_statement/reset_statement/comment_statement trees), grant/revoke named node types absent from all 321, and merge/truncate had no node type because their rules are hidden (`_merge_statement`, `_truncate_statement` inline into `statement`).
comment: This fixture is the pin on the whole dead-arm class: it is the only place in the repo where 'every arm is reachable' is asserted rather than assumed.

forbidRelationships.comment: a REVOKE ... FROM role privilege name is a ROLE, not a table a query reads; the pre-fix keyword-as-target defect published this row

note: `forbidRelationships` on `some_role` is the phantom-role pin: `REVOKE SELECT ON t FROM joe` put the ROLE name in a from clause and the analyzer reported `uses global->joe` — a role claimed as a table. The grammar half of the fix keeps grantees out of the reference space entirely; this is the analyzer-side assertion that it stayed fixed.
